content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the “EC2” terminology – that’s AWS.  
> * You must have the **Compute Engine API** enabled in your project.  
> * The zone you pick must support GPUs (e.g. `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.).  
> * You’ll need a service‑account key or OAuth token with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope.

---

## 1. `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Pick a zone that supports GPUs
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true   # optional: auto‑install driver
```

**What this does**

| Parameter | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM size |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| `--boot-disk-size` | 100 GB SSD boot disk |
| `--maintenance-policy=TERMINATE` | Instance will be terminated on host maintenance (GPU‑only) |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart if the VM crashes |

> **Tip** – If you want the NVIDIA driver installed automatically, set `install-nvidia-driver=true` in metadata.  
> For manual driver install, SSH into the VM and run `sudo ubuntu-drivers autoinstall`.

---

## 2. REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), use the following POST request.

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "install-nvidia-driver", "value": "true" }
    ]
  },
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE"
  }
}
```

### How to call it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> Replace `{PROJECT_ID}`, `{ZONE}`, and `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` with your values.  
> Save the JSON body above to `instance.json` before running the `curl` command.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| 1 | Enable Compute Engine API (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`) |
| 2 | Choose a GPU‑enabled zone (`gcloud compute zones list --filter="region:us-central1" --format="table(name,availableFeatures)"`) |
| 3 | Ensure you have the `nvidia-a6000` accelerator available in that zone |
| 4 | Create the instance (CLI or REST) |
| 5 | Verify GPU visibility inside the VM (`nvidia-smi`) |

That’s it! Once the instance is running, you can SSH in and start using the RTX A6000 for your workloads.
